The execution trace confirms the NS-4 condition failed (179 s), so the $6.61 was not chargeable and must be returned in full [F3][F7][NS-4].

The driver-side no-show branch cannot save the fee either. Where the driver's written statement ("waited more than 6 minutes … called twice") conflicts with the GPS and timeline records, the system records prevail, so that statement cannot support the fee [F10][F2][F4][NS-1]. NS-2 therefore applies and the $6.61 is refundable [F6][F2][NS-2].

The driver's profile (0 disputes, 0 upheld) also gives no basis for a repeated-violation referral under RD-6 [F15][RD-6], and profile facts cannot decide the case in any event [F14].

ruling.recommended_action: Refund the $6.61 cancellation fee to the rider as a Ryde voucher (NS-7); close the case with no account action.
ruling.reasoning:
The cancellation was made by the rider at 09:03:09, exactly 179 s (2 min 59 s) after acceptance at 09:00:10, and the $6.61 fee is the sole charge on record [F3][F7]. NS-0 routes a rider-side cancellation to NS-4, and NS-4 makes any cancellation within 3 minutes (≤ 3:00) of matching non-chargeable [F3][NS-0][NS-4]. The execution trace confirms the NS-4 condition failed (179 s), so the $6.61 was not chargeable and must be returned in full [F3][F7][NS-4].

The driver-side no-show branch cannot save the fee either. NS-1 requires all three of (i) an "I'm Here" tap, (ii) GPS presence at the pickup, and (iii) more than 3 minutes (≥ 3:01) of waiting within range [F2][F4][F5][NS-1]. The timeline is internally inconsistent — F5 records a tap at 09:03:00 while F6 records the tap field as null — but on either reading NS-1(iii) fails independently: the driver was inside 200 m for only 25 cumulative seconds before the cancellation, and only 29 s elapsed between the recorded arrival at 09:02:40 and the cancellation at 09:03:09 [F2][F4][F5][F6][NS-1]. Where the driver's written statement ("waited more than 6 minutes … called twice") conflicts with the GPS and timeline records, the system records prevail, so that statement cannot support the fee [F10][F2][F4][NS-1]. NS-2 therefore applies and the $6.61 is refundable [F6][F2][NS-2].

Amount: the trace fixes the refundable sum as the cancellation fee on record, $6.61 [F7][F8][NS-4][NS-7]. Per NS-7 the dispute was filed within 30 days and the refund is issued as a Ryde voucher, not cash [F7][NS-7].

No account action is warranted: the NS-2 flag_account trigger requires the driver to have pressed "I'm Here" while GPS showed him outside the pickup point, whereas here the GPS shows him within 39 m and within 200 m at the relevant times [F1][F2][F5][NS-2]. The driver's profile (0 disputes, 0 upheld) also gives no basis for a repeated-violation referral under RD-6 [F15][RD-6], and profile facts cannot decide the case in any event [F14].

rejected_claims.reason: The rider's 90-day profile (3 disputes, 0 upheld) is a profile fact and cannot decide anything on its own; the fee is refunded on the system-record timing under NS-4 (F3, F7), not because of the rider's history [F14][F3][NS-4].
Correct on the operative fact but it defeats the driver's position: cancellation 179 s after acceptance is inside the NS-4 free window, so the fee cannot stand as a rider-side charge [F3][NS-4].
Same effect: the absence of an 'I'm Here' tap (F6) plus only 25 s inside 200 m (F2) means NS-1 is unmet and NS-2 requires a full refund [F2][F6][NS-1][NS-2].

Accepted as to credibility only; the driver's 'more than 6 minutes' statement is contradicted by the GPS and timeline and loses to those system records, leaving no basis for the $6.61 [F10][F2][F4][NS-1].

The driver's clean 90-day record is a profile fact and cannot determine the fee; it is relevant only to account action, which is already not triggered because NS-2/NS-3 conditions for flagging are unmet [F15][NS-2][NS-3].

allowed outcomes: refund_full; amount = cancellation fee $6.61

claims.assertion: The rider cancelled 2 min 59 s after matching (09:00:10 → 09:03:09), i.e. within the 3-minute free-cancellation window, so no cancellation fee was chargeable.
The $6.61 cancellation fee was nevertheless charged and remains on record, so it must be refunded in full to the rider.

Even on the driver-side no-show branch, the driver's cumulative time within 200 m of the pickup before cancellation was only 25 s, far short of the required more-than-3-minute wait, so the fee cannot stand under NS-1.

The driver's written claim of waiting 'more than 6 minutes' at the stand is contradicted by the system record: he first came within 200 m of the pickup at 09:02:40 and cancellation followed 29 s later.
No in-app chat exists, so there is no recorded agreement or rider statement that could independently justify the fee; the driver's phone-call claim is unverifiable against any system record.
The rider's 90-day history shows no upheld disputes (0 of 3), so nothing in the profile supports treating this cancellation as abusive.

weaknesses: The rider did cancel, and by the counterfactual timing the margin is razor-thin: cancellation at 09:03:09 vs a 09:03:10 cut-off — the other side will argue the fee is a lawful 'after 3 minutes' charge (F3).
The driver did reach the pickup area (39 m at 09:03:00) and tapped 'I'm Here', so the driver will argue he was present and ready; only the duration, not his presence, defeats NS-1 (F1, F5).

The rider's own complaint admits she was 'two minutes away' when she messaged, which the driver will use to argue the rider, not the driver, caused the failed pickup (F9 shows no chat, so that admission rests on her statement alone).
The rider's profile shows 3 disputes in 90 days (0 upheld), which the driver may cite as a pattern of fee-waiver attempts (F14).

claims.assertion: The rider cancelled the trip herself at 09:03:09, 2 min 59 s after acceptance — still inside the 3-minute grace window on the face of the clock, so no cancellation fee could stand if that were the operative fact.

The timer that matters is the rider's cancellation right, not the driver's no-show claim: the driver never tapped "I'm Here" (driver_pressed_here_at is null), so the $6.61 cannot be justified under the passenger-no-show branch at all.
The GPS record shows the driver was within 200 m of the pickup for only 25 cumulative seconds before the cancellation — far short of the >180 s (≥3:01) required for a passenger no-show fee.

The driver's own written claim of waiting "more than 6 minutes at the stand" is contradicted by the system record: he first entered the 200 m radius at 09:02:40 and the rider cancelled 29 s later, so the statement cannot carry the fee.
There is no in-app chat in which the rider agreed to any routing change or extended wait, so no alternative contractual basis for the $6.61 exists in the message record.
No service type is recorded and no toll, waiting-fee or extra-distance item was added to the bill — the sole charge on record is the $6.61 cancellation fee, so the disputed amount is exactly $6.61.

The driver's 90-day record (0 disputes, 0 upheld, 4.9 rating over 700 trips) shows this is an isolated timing issue rather than a pattern of cancellation-fee abuse, so no account-level action against him is warranted.

weaknesses: The strongest fact for the other side is F3: cancellation at 09:03:09 is 2 min 59 s after 09:00:10 acceptance, i.e. within the NS-4 free-cancellation window, and the rider's counterfactual (179 s) matches it — the rider will argue this alone settles the case regardless of the driver's conduct.

One timeline entry (F5) records the driver tapping "I'm Here" at 09:03:00, 39 m from the pickup; that contrasts with F6 (null tap) and with my own claim D2, and the judge may prefer F5 and then test NS-1(iii) — which still fails on F2's 25 s, but the inconsistency weakens the credibility of the 'no tap' argument.

The driver's chat statement (F10) asserting a 6-minute wait is factually wrong against F2/F4 and invites an adverse credibility finding, which could also invite an NS-2 style flag_account argument for button misuse if the judge accepts F5 over F6.
A refund here is a $6.61 voucher (NS-7), so the practical exposure is small and the judge may see little harm in granting it, making my client's position hard to defend on proportionality grounds.

points.response: Concede — the 2 min 59 s interval in F3 puts the cancellation inside the NS-4 window and my client is entitled to full refund of the $6.61; the driver's advocate agrees on this operative fact.
Concede; the driver-side no-show branch adds nothing to my case, since F6 records no 'I'm Here' tap and NS-1(i) therefore fails independently.

Adopt: F2's 25 cumulative seconds inside 200 m before cancellation is far below the >180 s required by NS-1(iii), and F4 shows only 29 s elapsed after recorded arrival — the fee is unsupportable on the driver's own evidence.
Adopt, and press it further: F10's 'more than 6 minutes' wait is contradicted by F2/F4, so the driver's credibility on the wait cannot outweigh the system record under NS-1.
Adopt: F9 records no in-app messages at all, so there is no agreement, no routing variation and no alternative basis for charging my client, leaving only NS-4 which bars the fee.
Adopt: F7 shows $6.61 as the sole contested charge and F8 confirms 1.0x surge, so the exact sum to be refunded is $6.61 with no deduction.
I do not seek any account action against the driver — my client's request is limited to the $6.61 refund, so F15 is irrelevant to the relief sought (F7).

Conceded on the rider-cancellation branch: F3 shows cancellation at 09:03:09, 2 min 59 s after the 09:00:10 acceptance, inside the NS-4 three-minute no-charge window, so the $6.61 cannot be sustained as a rider-side cancellation fee.

The amount and the refund route are not in dispute — only $6.61 appears on the record (F7, with no surge at F8) and any return is a voucher under NS-7 — but the refund is owed because NS-1 fails, not because a free cancellation window was available to a rider the driver never charged under NS-1.

Agreed and independently fatal to the fee: F6 records that the driver never tapped "I'm Here" (driver_pressed_here_at is null), so NS-1(i) is unmet even before the 25-second figure in F2 defeats NS-1(iii).
Conceded: F10 is my client's own statement and it is contradicted by the system record in F2 and F4, so the "more than 6 minutes" assertion carries no weight.

F9 confirms there is no in-app chat (my client's two phone calls appear only in his own statement, F10, which loses to the GPS/timeline record), and that absence equally deprives my client of any RD-3/NS-1-adjacent basis for the fee.

The rider's profile (F14, 3 disputes, 0 upheld) cannot decide anything under NS-4; equally, my client's clean record (F15, 0 disputes over 700 trips, rating 4.9) means this timing error should not be escalated as fee abuse, and NS-2's flag_account is not triggered here.

notices.text:
You were charged a $6.61 cancellation fee. We're refunding it in full as a Ryde voucher, not cash.

What decided it: you cancelled about 3 minutes after a driver accepted, which is inside the window where cancelling is free. The driver's waiting time and location records also didn't meet the standard needed to keep the fee.

Nothing changes on your account. The voucher will appear in your Ryde account balance and applies to your next trip.

We reviewed the $6.61 cancellation fee from this trip and are refunding it to the rider as a Ryde voucher.

What decided it: the rider cancelled about 3 minutes after you accepted, inside the free-cancellation window. Your arrival and in-range records also didn't show the waiting time required to keep the fee, and where your statement differed from the trip records, the records were used.

No action is being taken against your account over this trip, so nothing changes for you going forward.
